title: Omni-Safety under Cross-Modality Conflict: Vulnerabilities, Dynamic Mechanisms and Efficient Alignment
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Seed data is transformed along two parallel paths, single-modal rendering and multi-modal semantic separation, into a combined multi-subset benchmark.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, two stacked color-coded branches merging into a dataset panel
description: A left-to-right dataset construction diagram. At the far left, a gray box labeled Seed Data AdvBench holds a book icon and the text '520 Malicious, 500 Benign Queries'. Blue arrows lead to the top-center panel, 'Single-Modal Transformation (Direct Rendering)'. It renders a query into image/video (a monitor showing 'How to make a bomb?') and audio via TTS (a speaker), and these outputs fan out into Pure Image, Pure Video and Pure Audio boxes. An orange arrow leads through a scissors icon to the bottom-center panel, 'Multi-Modal Transformation (Semantic Separation Strategy)'. It splits the query into Path A (text context) and Path B (a visual/audio payload, 'bomb'), and these combine into Text+Image, Text+Audio and Text+Video+Audio boxes. A large pink arrow points to the right panel, 'AdvBench-Omni'. That panel lists 11 modality subsets (T, I, A, V, T+I, T+A and so on) as icons, with 'Total: 11,220 Samples' at the bottom. Blue, orange and pink distinguish the stages.
caption: The construction pipeline of AdvBench-Omni.
abstract: Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs) greatly expand LLMs' multimodal capabilities but also introduce cross-modal safety risks. However, a systematic understanding of vulnerabilities in omni-modal interactions remains lacking. To bridge this gap, we establish a modality-semantics decoupling principle and construct the AdvBench-Omni dataset, which reveals a significant vulnerability in OLLMs. Mechanistic analysis uncovers a Mid-layer Dissolution phenomenon driven by refusal vector magnitude shrinkage, alongside the existence of a modal-invariant pure refusal direction. Inspired by these insights, we extract a golden refusal vector using Singular Value Decomposition and propose OmniSteer, which utilizes lightweight adapters to modulate intervention intensity adaptively. Extensive experiments show that our method not only increases the Refusal Success Rate against harmful inputs from 69.9% to 91.2%, but also effectively preserves the general capabilities across all modalities. Our code is available at: https://github.com/zhrli324/omni-safety-research.
